_why_windows_powershell: CORRECTED 2026-09-15 -- the 2026-08-15 note below is WRONG and is kept only for history; do not trust its premise. It claimed a J-opened WindowsTerminal's title reads the hosted shell's full path (so 'Windows PowerShell', with a space, would discriminate it from an automation shell's path-with-no-space title). Checked live against window-leaks.jsonl and window-leak-hook logs on 2026-09-15: WindowsTerminal.exe's window title is almost always its own generic 'Terminal' (WT app title, not the shell's), never once observed as 'Windows PowerShell' in ~5,200 logged rows, and a WTSGetActiveConsoleSessionId() check plus live ancestry inspection confirmed J's own interactive WindowsTerminal is BYTE-IDENTICAL (ancestry AND session id) to a scheduled-task-spawned one on this box. No signal available to window_leak_hook.py / window-leak-detector.py can safely tell them apart. FIX SHIPPED 2026-09-15: WindowsTerminal.exe and its OpenConsole.exe conpty host are now structurally excluded from BOTH scripts' auto-hide path (see CONSOLE_HOST_IMAGES / CONSOLE_HOST in each file) -- they are logged for leak-awareness but never ShowWindow(SW_HIDE)'d, full stop. This allowlist's title_substrings still apply to WindowsTerminal.exe's title as defense-in-depth (harmless if it never matches) but are NOT the load-bearing safety mechanism anymore -- the code-level exclusion is. The original 2026-08-15 rationale text is preserved below verbatim for audit trail: 'ADDED 2026-08-15 after the detector hid J's own interactive PowerShell window twice at 18:03 ET. The ancestry safety gate is NOT buggy -- its premise is. Modern Windows Terminal launches by DCOM activation, so a terminal J opens from the Start menu is spawned by svchost.exe -> services.exe -> wininit.exe with NO explorer.exe anywhere: byte-identical to the service-rooted leak signature. Ancestry therefore cannot distinguish J's terminal from a Task Scheduler leak, and the title allowlist (already honoured for WindowsTerminal.exe) is the intended discriminator. The space matters: automation-spawned shells are titled with a FULL PATH ("C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe" -- "WindowsPowerShell", no space), so this substring exempts the interactive window WITHOUT exempting them. Verified against the real window-leaks.jsonl records.' -- that verification step evidently used a fixture, not the live title field; live rows contradict it.
